category_title: Adolescent with Down's syndrome engaging in verbal outbursts
minimal_context: Dennis is sitting one-on-one with a tutor in his classroom to practice tracing and writing letters.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Dennis, let's start your writing activity. Please trace the letters on this paper.

STUDENT: (Shakes head) No.

TUTOR: Pick up your pencil and try the first one.

STUDENT: (Pushes the pencil away) Stop it.

TUTOR: We need to finish tracing these letters.

STUDENT: (Points across the room) He talking! That’s enough!

options.A: Assign two to five letters per month to learn and ask the student to identify the letters at the end of the month.
options.B: Conduct functional analyses in the setting where the behavior naturally occurs by embedding trials into the student's daily classroom activities.
options.C: Show the student how to use a sensory tool appropriately (e.g., keep it in his hands, set it on the desk, or squeeze it when anxious).
options.D: Provide extra time to complete the letter-tracing assignments, allowing for flexibility with timelines during the daily classroom activities.
